Now, I undertsand @Atko and @PuttItOut are busy people, but in light of the recent @henrycorp and some other power mods' actions lately, I've been thinking of some ways to give users of subverses some more power.

One idea I had was to allow users to vote to kick a moderator out, and then vote to instill a new one. Now, some problems with this (Besides those good site owners mentioned above having to somehow implement this) could be bot vote manipulation, also mob mentality, if a mod happens to make a mistake or unpopular one-time choice or something along those lines, the internet is a fickle beasty.

Now, the above idea is still a legitimate one (besides its flaws) but it got me thinking, instead of having all users vote, perhaps allow subverses to have a set number(maybe three) of moderators no matter what, if a subverse has below this number, the users can vote for people to be made mods, and of course those people can decline if they so wish, THEN, since the mods were voted in by the users, the mods could keep each other in line by being allowed to vote to kick another mod out. Now, to prevent hostile takeovers of subverses, IF somehow TWO moderators with a similar hostile agenda got elected and tried to vote to kick an innocent mod out, THEN users get to vote if this verdict by the two mods should pass. This way there's a round-a-bout checks and balances system. Now, this isn't perfect, if someone was REALLY good at manipulation and had no life, they could theoretically convince a subverse that their two account are different people, happen to win out and get them elected, vote to ban the innocent mod, use bots as the userbase to vote said mod out, and take over, but I think the above system can stop MOST if not all attempts of this. There's still the problem of having to implement such a system somehow site-wide.

Let me know your thoughts, this is just my own brainstorming all smashed into a wall of text, maybe you guys (who are much smarter than me) can revise my ideas into something feasible. Cheers!
